candidates.proposedShortDesc: RNA-seq of M. oryzae pkc1AS mycelium with and without the inhibitor 1NA-PP1.
candidates.uncertainty: The readme says three biological replicates while pkc_summary.docx says two per timepoint; omit a replicate count. No owner attribution is inferred.

clues: A strain of M. oryzae was constructed in which the native PKC1 gene was replaced with an analogue-sensitive PKC1 allele (pkc1AS). This allele could be inhbited by the analogue 1NA-PP1. Global transcriptional profiling of mycelium following selective PKC inhibition identified significant changes in gene expression associated with cell wall re-modelling, autophagy, signal transduction and secondary metabolism.
Mycelium was grown in the presence and absence (control) of the inhibitor 1NA-PP1 for a number of different times up to 24 hours.
A, B and D correspond to three biological replicates.

Mycelium grown in shaking culture. PKC inhibitor added and samples of mycelium harvested at time intervals of up to 24 hours from which RNA was extracted (for RNA-Seq). Compared with control in which inhibitor was not added to mycelium. Two replicates for each timepoint. RNA-Seq analysis performed using DESeq.
Heat map showing distance between samples (replicates from same condition should cluster together)

candidates.proposedLongDesc: RNA-seq of M. oryzae carrying an analogue-sensitive PKC1 allele (pkc1AS). Mycelium was sampled with and without 1NA-PP1 at time points up to 24 hours to examine transcriptional responses to PKC1 inhibition. Historical project number: 2035.
